title: Methodist church, New Orleans University, leaving at sixteen, first dances
summary: Religion and school through his minister grandfather, church music, leaving New Orleans at sixteen after playing unpaid dances with drums and piano.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Yeah. I wondered, which church did you belong to? Did you hear any special music in the churches? Were you Catholic or Protestant?

No, I was Methodist at that time. That's a good point you brought up because, to my knowledge, most all the musicians have some faith in my grandfather as a minister. You were the minister? Yes. Mm-hmm.
Do you remember any of the music in the churches when you were a boy?

Oh, yes. In my school they still sing. I'm now in the churches. Same standard church number. But the numbers of bands are playing nowadays, why they wasn't using them during those times. Yeah. Mm-hmm. I attended New Orleans University.
Oh, yes. At Penesbury, right? Yes. That's the one up on St. Charles? That's right. You went way up to that? Yeah.

Well, they didn't have to pay for me to go to school because my grandfather was a minister, so I ain't got it bad. Oh, I see. Is that a Methodist school? Yeah, that's a Methodist. You are a Methodist person?
Yeah. Yeah. That's a Methodist school, since y'all have been on T. Yeah.
How old were you when you left New Orleans? About? Sixteen.
You did play a few dances then?
Well, we call them dances, yes. I didn't get paid for it, but I went and played anyway. It's just how I didn't get to play.
Do you remember the other musicians that were in the band?
Well, they had a drum and a piano and clarinet. That was all. There wasn't no bands then.
Do you remember the other fellows? There were any of them?

I can't recall the piano player now. How I got to play it, Pete Lawless was through larynge. He was sick. They wanted somebody, because I guess I was taking lessons from his father. I couldn't play near as good as he could. Because he had the C clarinet and he played all the melody. And I didn't, never learn to play strictly melody. Yeah.
